source: Four Little Chicks and the Siberian Crane
Lali faces the rising Sun on the school ground. She then tur

items.question: Lali faces the rising Sun on the school ground. She then turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. Which direction is she facing now, and which direction is behind her?
steps: Lali faces the rising Sun. The rising Sun is in the east, so she faces east.
Facing east, her left hand points north and her right hand points south.
She turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. That is north, so she now faces north.
Behind her is the opposite of north. North and south are opposite directions, so south is behind her.
Check: north is at the top of the compass rose and south is at the bottom, so they are opposite directions.
items.answer: She is facing north, and south is behind her

videos.answer: She is facing north, and south is behind her

source: Finding Directions: Manu and the rising Sun

items.question: Manu is facing the rising Sun. That direction is ___. His left hand is pointing in the ___ direction. His right hand is pointing in the ___ direction.
steps: Manu faces the rising Sun. The rising Sun is in the east, so Manu faces east. The first blank is east.
Manu stretches both arms out to the sides. Facing east, his left hand points north. The second blank is north.
His right hand points the opposite way, south. The third blank is south.
Check: his two hands point in opposite directions, north and south, and east is in front of him.
items.answer: East, north, south. Manu faces east, his left hand points north and his right hand points south.

videos.answer: East, north, south. Manu faces east, his left hand points north and his right hand points south.

source: Finding Directions: which way is west

items.question: Which way is west?
steps: Manu faces east, the direction of the rising Sun.
West is the direction opposite to east, so it is behind him.
Check: his left hand is north and his right hand is south, so west is the one direction left, behind him.
items.answer: West is behind Manu, opposite to the rising Sun, which is in the east.

videos.answer: West is behind Manu, opposite to the rising Sun, which is in the east.

source: A playground picture has a compass with N at the top. A swin

items.question: A playground picture has a compass with N at the top. A swing is at the top left, a slide at the top right, a sandpit at the bottom left and a seesaw at the bottom right. Which thing is east of the swing, south of the slide, west of the seesaw and north of the sandpit?
steps: The compass has N at the top, so above is north, below is south, the right is east and the left is west.
East of the swing: look to the right of the swing. The slide is there.
South of the slide: look below the slide. The seesaw is there.
West of the seesaw: look to the left of the seesaw. The sandpit is there.
North of the sandpit: look above the sandpit. The swing is there.
Check: the swing and the slide are in the top row and the sandpit and the seesaw are in the bottom row, and the top row is north of the bottom row.
items.answer: The slide is east of the swing, the seesaw is south of the slide, the sandpit is west of the seesaw and the swing is north of the sandpit

videos.answer: The slide is east of the swing, the seesaw is south of the slide, the sandpit is west of the seesaw and the swing is north of the sandpit

source: A girl stands at the centre of a room plan with a compass, N

items.question: A girl stands at the centre of a room plan with a compass, N at the top. A table is above her, a bed is to the right of her, a door is below her and a cupboard is to the left of her. Say the direction of each thing from the girl. Then say in which direction the girl is from the bed.
steps: N is at the top, so above is north, the right is east, below is south and the left is west.
The table is above her, so the table is north of her.
The bed is to the right of her, so the bed is east of her.
The door is below her, so the door is south of her.
The cupboard is to the left of her, so the cupboard is west of her.
Now stand at the bed and look at the girl. She is to the left of the bed, so she is west of the bed.
Check: the bed is east of the girl and the girl is west of the bed, and east and west are opposite directions.
items.answer: The table is north, the bed east, the door south and the cupboard west of the girl. From the bed the girl is to the west

videos.answer: The table is north, the bed east, the door south and the cupboard west of the girl. From the bed the girl is to the west

source: Bird Watching: colour the tents

items.question: Children are at a bird-watching camp. Read the clues and colour the tents in the camp accordingly. The tent to the west of the road is blue. The tent closest to the lake is green. The tent north of the green tent is purple. The tent south of the lake is yellow.
steps: Find the compass. N is at the top, so above is north, below is south, left is west and right is east.
Clue 1: the tent to the west of the road is blue. West is to the left, so colour blue the tent on the left of the road.
Clue 2: the tent closest to the lake is green. Colour green the tent just above the lake.
Clue 3: the tent north of the green tent is purple. North is above, so colour purple the tent above the green tent, near the top.
Clue 4: the tent south of the lake is yellow. South is below, so colour yellow the tent below the lake.
Check: there are four clues and four tents, and each tent has its own colour: blue, green, purple and yellow.
items.answer: Blue: the tent left of the road. Green: the tent just above the lake. Purple: the tent above the green tent. Yellow: the tent below the lake.

videos.answer: Blue: the tent left of the road. Green: the tent just above the lake. Purple: the tent above the green tent. Yellow: the tent below the lake.

source: Bird Watching: a tent east of the lake

items.question: Now, draw a tent to the east of the lake.
steps: The compass has E on the right, so east is to the right.
Find the lake. East of the lake is the ground on the right side of the lake.
Draw a tent there, on the right of the lake and away from the water.
Check: the tent is to the right of the lake, so the lake is to the west of the tent.
items.answer: Sample answer: a tent drawn on the ground to the right of the lake. Your answer may differ: any place to the right of the lake is right.

videos.answer: Sample answer: a tent drawn on the ground to the right of the lake. Your answer may differ: any place to the right of the lake is right.

source: Map of a Room: directions from the girl

items.question: Write the directions of the following in relation to the girl. Window ___ Bed ___ Cupboard ___ Bedside table ___
steps: On the compass, N is at the top. In the picture, up towards the back wall is north, the right is east, the left is west and towards us is south.
Window: it is on the back wall, behind the girl, so it is north of her.
Bed: it is on the right side of the picture, so it is east of her.
Cupboard: it is on the back wall at the left, a little behind her, so the nearest direction is west.
Bedside table: it is the round table beside the bed, in front of her and a little to the right, so the nearest direction is south.
Check: the cupboard and the bedside table sit between two directions. We use only four directions, so we name the nearest one. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: Sample answer: window north, bed east, cupboard west, bedside table south. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: window north, bed east, cupboard west, bedside table south. Your answer may differ.

source: Map of a Room: draw your room

items.question: Make a drawing of your room and locate the direction in which different things have been placed in relation to you standing at the centre of the room. Make the direction arrow for your room.
steps: Draw your room as a square seen from above. Mark yourself with a dot at the centre.
Find north. Face the rising Sun, which is east. North is on your left hand.
Draw the direction arrow in a corner: N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left, and draw the room so that north is at the top.
Draw each thing where it stands as seen from the dot. In a sample room the window is on the north wall, the bed on the east side, the cupboard on the west side and the door on the south wall.
Write the direction of each thing from you: window north, bed east, cupboard west, door south.
Check: each thing sits on the side of the square that matches its direction. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: Sample answer: window north, bed east, cupboard west, door south, with a direction arrow. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: window north, bed east, cupboard west, door south, with a direction arrow. Your answer may differ.

source: Map of a Room: names in the four directions

items.question: Write the names of the things that are placed in the following directions. East ___ West ___ North ___ South ___
steps: Look at your drawing from the dot at the centre.
East is the right side. In the sample room the bed is there.
West is the left side. In the sample room the cupboard is there.
North is the top. In the sample room the window is there.
South is the bottom. In the sample room the door is there.
Check: each thing is on the side of the square that matches its direction. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: Sample answer: East: bed. West: cupboard. North: window. South: door. Your answer may differ, it depends on your room.

videos.answer: Sample answer: East: bed. West: cupboard. North: window. South: door. Your answer may differ, it depends on your room.

source: What is just south of the Basketball Court, across Market Ro

items.question: What is just south of the Basketball Court, across Market Road, and what is just north of it?
steps: A street map is a picture of roads and places seen from above. The compass has N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left.
Find the Basketball Court in the middle of the map. Market Road runs along the bottom of the court.
Go down the map, across Market Road. Down the map is south, so the place just south of the Basketball Court is the Shopping Centre.
Now go up the map from the court, across the small road above it. Up the map is north, so just north of the court is the block with the pond and Jaideep's House.
Turn it round. If the Shopping Centre is south of the court, then the court is north of the Shopping Centre.
Check with the compass: up is N, so north is up the map and south is down the map.
items.answer: The Shopping Centre is just south of the Basketball Court. The block with the pond and Jaideep's House is just north of it.

videos.answer: The Shopping Centre is just south of the Basketball Court. The block with the pond and Jaideep's House is just north of it.

source: A cycle drives north along a road and turns left at a juncti

items.question: A cycle drives north along a road and turns left at a junction. Which direction is it driving after the turn? At the next junction it turns left again. Which direction is it driving now?
steps: The cycle drives north. Face north: your left hand points west and your right hand points east.
A left turn is a turn towards the left hand. The left hand points west, so after the first turn the cycle drives west.
Now the cycle drives west. Face west: your left hand points south.
The second left turn is towards south, so the cycle now drives south.
Check with the rule: a left turn takes north to west, and west to south.
The two left turns together made the cycle drive the opposite way to the way it started: it started north and now drives south.
items.answer: After the first left turn the cycle drives west. After the second left turn it drives south

videos.answer: After the first left turn the cycle drives west. After the second left turn it drives south

source: Bus Route: Stop 1

items.question: The bus will start from the parking area. It will go north and then it will take a right turn onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction to reach Stop 1 (S1).
steps: Find the PARKING area at the bottom of the map. The red dotted route goes up the map from there, and up the map is north.
Near the top of the map the route meets the road with the Hospital above it. The name on that road is Hospital Road.
The bus drives north and takes a right turn. A right turn changes north to east, so the bus drives east along Hospital Road.
Stop 1 is at the hospital gate on Hospital Road, so the bus reaches Stop 1 driving east.
Check: the red arrows on Hospital Road point to the right, and the compass has E on the right.
items.answer: The blanks are Hospital and east. The bus turns right onto Hospital Road driving east.

videos.answer: The blanks are Hospital and east. The bus turns right onto Hospital Road driving east.

source: Bus Route: Stop 2

items.question: To reach Stop 2 (S2), it will turn ___ (right/left) onto ___ Road driving in the ___ direction.
steps: The bus is driving east on Hospital Road. It goes on east until it meets the road down the right side of the map. That road is Park Road.
The route now goes down the map. Down the map is south.
The bus changes from driving east to driving south. A right turn changes east to south, so the turn is a right turn.
Stop 2 is beside the Shopping Centre, near the south end of Park Road, so the bus reaches Stop 2 driving south.
Check: facing east, your right hand points south.
items.answer: The blanks are right, Park and south. The bus turns right onto Park Road driving south.

videos.answer: The blanks are right, Park and south. The bus turns right onto Park Road driving south.

source: Street Map: east of Jaideep's house

items.question: Whose houses are situated to the east of Jaideep's house? ___
steps: Find Jaideep's House in the middle of the map, below Tinku's House and Golu's House.
East is to the right of Jaideep's House. Look across Park Road, the road down the right side.
On the east side of Park Road are two houses near the height of Jaideep's House: Prem's House a little higher and Raju's House a little lower.
Check with the compass: E is on the right, and Prem's House and Raju's House are the houses to the right of Park Road.
items.answer: Prem's house and Raju's house.

videos.answer: Prem's house and Raju's house.

source: Street Map: Ravi's house to the park

items.question: Mark the route from Ravi's house to the children's park.
steps: Find Ravi's House on the left side of the map and the Children's Park at the top right. The gate of Ravi's House opens to the south, onto a small road.
Go south out of the gate to the small road, then turn left and go east along it to the main road on the left.
Turn left and go north up the main road, all the way to Hospital Road.
Turn right and go east along Hospital Road to Park Road. The Children's Park is on the east side of Park Road, at the top right.
Check: every part of the route is on a road, and it ends at the Children's Park.
Your answer may differ: other routes along the roads are right too.
items.answer: Sample answer: south to the small road, east to the main road, north to Hospital Road, east to Park Road and the park. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: south to the small road, east to the main road, north to Hospital Road, east to Park Road and the park. Your answer may differ.

source: Street Map: the stop closer to Lali's house

items.question: Which stop is closer to Lali's house? ___
steps: Find Lali's House at the top left of the map.
Find the two stops. Stop 1 is at the hospital gate on Hospital Road, near the top of the map. Stop 2 is beside the Shopping Centre, near the bottom right.
From Lali's House, Stop 1 is a short way along Hospital Road to the east. Stop 2 is a long way, down the map and over to the right.
No distances are printed on the map, so we judge from the picture. Stop 1 is closer.
Check: Stop 1 is at about the same height as Lali's House, near the top, and Stop 2 is at the bottom.
items.answer: Stop 1.

videos.answer: Stop 1.

source: Street Map: Golu runs late

items.question: Golu is running late. Trace the route to help him reach the nearest bus stop.
steps: Find Golu's House just below Hospital Road. Stop 1 is at the hospital gate, close above it. Stop 2 is far away at the bottom right. The nearest stop is Stop 1.
The gate of Golu's House opens to the south, onto the road below the house. Go south out of the gate to that road.
Turn left and go east along the road to Park Road.
Turn left and go north up Park Road to Hospital Road.
Turn left and go west along Hospital Road to the hospital gate, where Stop 1 stands.
Check: the route stays on the roads and ends at Stop 1. The way along the left main road is longer.
Your answer may differ: other routes along the roads to Stop 1 are right too.
items.answer: Sample answer: south to the road below, east to Park Road, north to Hospital Road, west to Stop 1. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: south to the road below, east to Park Road, north to Hospital Road, west to Stop 1. Your answer may differ.

source: Street Map: Prem to Stop 2

items.question: In which direction would Prem have to move to reach Stop 2?
steps: Find Prem's House on the east side of Park Road, on the right of the map.
Find Stop 2 beside the Shopping Centre, near the bottom of the map.
Stop 2 is below Prem's House, so Prem has to move down the map. Down the map is south.
Stop 2 is also a little to the left of Prem's House, but this chapter uses only the four directions, so the nearest direction is south.
Check with the compass: S is at the bottom, and Stop 2 is at the bottom of the map.
items.answer: South. Stop 2 is below Prem's house.

videos.answer: South. Stop 2 is below Prem's house.

source: On the metro map, look at Hauz Khas. Which two lines meet th

items.question: On the metro map, look at Hauz Khas. Which two lines meet there, and how do you know you can change lines there?
steps: Find Hauz Khas in the lower middle of the metro map. Its symbol is not a plain circle. It is a capsule with two coloured dots.
The two dots are yellow and magenta. In the key, the yellow colour is the Yellow Line and the magenta colour is the Magenta Line.
Now read the key. Symbol 9, a plain circle, is a Metro Station. Symbol 10, a capsule with two coloured dots, is an Interchange Line.
So Hauz Khas is an interchange. The Yellow Line and the Magenta Line meet there, and you can change from one line to the other.
Check: the capsule has two dots, one dot for each line that meets there.
items.answer: The Yellow Line and the Magenta Line meet at Hauz Khas. Its symbol is the interchange capsule from the key, so you can change lines there

videos.answer: The Yellow Line and the Magenta Line meet at Hauz Khas. Its symbol is the interchange capsule from the key, so you can change lines there

source: Ride the Magenta Line from Hauz Khas to Kalkaji Mandir, chan

items.question: Ride the Magenta Line from Hauz Khas to Kalkaji Mandir, change to the Violet Line and ride on to Badarpur. How many stations are between Hauz Khas and Kalkaji Mandir, and between Kalkaji Mandir and Badarpur?
steps: Start at Hauz Khas and ride along the Magenta Line towards Kalkaji Mandir. Count only the circles between the two stations, not the two ends.
There are 4 circles between Hauz Khas and Kalkaji Mandir, so 4 stations between them.
Kalkaji Mandir is a capsule with a magenta dot and a violet dot. The Magenta Line and the Violet Line meet there, so we change lines at Kalkaji Mandir.
Now ride along the Violet Line towards Badarpur. There are 6 circles between Kalkaji Mandir and Badarpur, so 6 stations between them.
In all, between Hauz Khas and Badarpur there are 4 stations, then Kalkaji Mandir, then 6 stations: 4 + 1 + 6 = 11 stations.
Check: the capsule counts as one station, and we did not count Hauz Khas or Badarpur, the two ends.
items.answer: There are 4 stations between Hauz Khas and Kalkaji Mandir, and 6 between Kalkaji Mandir and Badarpur. In all, 4 + 1 + 6 = 11 stations between Hauz Khas and Badarpur

videos.answer: There are 4 stations between Hauz Khas and Kalkaji Mandir, and 6 between Kalkaji Mandir and Badarpur. In all, 4 + 1 + 6 = 11 stations between Hauz Khas and Badarpur

source: Metro Map: the coloured lines

items.question: What do the different coloured lines represent?
steps: Read the key at the bottom right of the map. Symbols 1 to 8 are coloured lines: Red, Yellow, Blue, Airport Express, Green, Violet, Pink and Magenta.
Find each colour on the map. A coloured line passes through a row of circles, and each circle is a metro station on that line.
Each coloured line is a different metro route. The colours make it easier to find and follow a route.
Check: the key has 8 coloured lines, and the map has 8 colours of line.
items.answer: Each coloured line is a different metro route: Red, Yellow, Blue, Airport Express, Green, Violet, Pink and Magenta. The colour tells which route a station is on.

videos.answer: Each coloured line is a different metro route: Red, Yellow, Blue, Airport Express, Green, Violet, Pink and Magenta. The colour tells which route a station is on.

source: Metro Map: mark two stations

items.question: Mark the Qutb Minar station on the Yellow Line and the Supreme Court station on the Blue Line.
steps: Find the Yellow Line. It is the yellow line that runs from the bottom left up the middle of the map.
Follow it up from the bottom left. The labelled circle Qutb Minar is on the lower part of the Yellow Line, and the next station up the line is Saket. Mark Qutb Minar with a ring.
Find the Blue Line. Rajiv Chowk is a capsule where the Blue Line meets the Yellow Line. Follow the Blue Line to the right of Rajiv Chowk.
The third station after Rajiv Chowk is Supreme Court, the labelled circle between Rajiv Chowk and Yamuna Bank. Mark Supreme Court with a ring.
Check: Qutb Minar is on the Yellow Line, Supreme Court is on the Blue Line, and both names are printed beside their circles.
items.answer: Qutb Minar: the labelled circle on the lower part of the Yellow Line, next to Saket. Supreme Court: the labelled circle on the Blue Line, third after Rajiv Chowk.

videos.answer: Qutb Minar: the labelled circle on the lower part of the Yellow Line, next to Saket. Supreme Court: the labelled circle on the Blue Line, third after Rajiv Chowk.

source: Metro Routes: trace the routes

items.question: Look at the metro map and trace different routes from the Qutb Minar metro station to the Supreme Court metro station.
steps: Start at Qutb Minar on the Yellow Line. Supreme Court is on the Blue Line, so every route must change to the Blue Line. We can change only at a capsule.
Route A: ride the Yellow Line up to Rajiv Chowk, change to the Blue Line there, and ride to Supreme Court. This route has one change.
Route B: ride the Yellow Line to INA, change to the Pink Line and ride to Mayur Vihar, then change to the Blue Line and ride to Supreme Court. This route has two changes.
Route C: ride the Yellow Line to Hauz Khas, change to the Magenta Line and ride to Botanical Garden, then change to the Blue Line and ride to Supreme Court. This route has two changes.
Check each change: Rajiv Chowk, INA, Mayur Vihar, Hauz Khas and Botanical Garden are all capsules that show the colours of both lines.
Your answer may differ: other routes on the map are right too.
items.answer: Sample answer: A, Yellow to Rajiv Chowk, then Blue. B, Yellow to INA, Pink to Mayur Vihar, then Blue. C, Yellow to Hauz Khas, Magenta to Botanical Garden, then Blue.

videos.answer: Sample answer: A, Yellow to Rajiv Chowk, then Blue. B, Yellow to INA, Pink to Mayur Vihar, then Blue. C, Yellow to Hauz Khas, Magenta to Botanical Garden, then Blue.

source: Metro Routes: Lali's suggestion

items.question: Lali says, "We can take the Yellow Line and change the metro at Hauz Khas to take the Magenta Line." If the children follow Lali's suggestion, at which station(s) do they need to change the metro line again to reach the Supreme Court metro station?
steps: Lali's plan: ride the Yellow Line from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas and change there to the Magenta Line.
Ride the Magenta Line to the right on the map. It passes Kalkaji Mandir, a capsule where the Violet Line meets it, but the children stay on the Magenta Line, so they need no change there.
The Magenta Line meets the Blue Line at the capsule Botanical Garden, which has a magenta dot and a blue dot. They change there to the Blue Line.
Ride the Blue Line to Supreme Court. So the children change again at Botanical Garden.
The Magenta Line also runs the other way from Hauz Khas, to Janakpuri West, where it meets the Blue Line. That way is much longer: 31 stations between instead of 25.
Check: Botanical Garden is a capsule that shows the colours of both lines, Magenta and Blue.
items.answer: Botanical Garden, where the Magenta Line meets the Blue Line. The other way, at Janakpuri West, is much longer.

videos.answer: Botanical Garden, where the Magenta Line meets the Blue Line. The other way, at Janakpuri West, is much longer.

source: Metro Routes: the fewest stations

items.question: Which route has the least number of stations between Qutb Minar and Supreme Court?
steps: Count the stations between Qutb Minar and Supreme Court on each route. A capsule where we change counts as one station. Do not count Qutb Minar or Supreme Court.

Route A: count the circles on the Yellow Line from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas (2), Hauz Khas (1), then 2 to INA, INA (1), 3 to Central Secretariat, Central Secretariat (1), 1 to Rajiv Chowk, Rajiv Chowk (1), then 2 on the Blue Line to Supreme Court. 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 14.
Route B: 5 stations from Qutb Minar to INA, INA (1), 5 on the Pink Line to Mayur Vihar, Mayur Vihar (1), 1 to Yamuna Bank, Yamuna Bank (1), 1 to Supreme Court. 5 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 15.

Route C: 3 stations from Qutb Minar to Hauz Khas, 4 on the Magenta Line to Kalkaji Mandir, Kalkaji Mandir (1), 7 to Botanical Garden, Botanical Garden (1), 5 on the Blue Line to Mayur Vihar, Mayur Vihar (1), 1 to Yamuna Bank, Yamuna Bank (1), 1 to Supreme Court. 3 + 4 + 1 + 7 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 25.
14 is less than 15, and 15 is less than 25, so Route A has the fewest stations between.
Check: Route A changes at Rajiv Chowk, the capsule where the Yellow Line meets the Blue Line, so it stays on the Yellow Line the longest.
items.answer: Route A: the Yellow Line to Rajiv Chowk, then the Blue Line. It has 14 stations between, fewer than Route B (15) and Route C (25).

videos.answer: Route A: the Yellow Line to Rajiv Chowk, then the Blue Line. It has 14 stations between, fewer than Route B (15) and Route C (25).

source: Metro Routes: the best way to the zoo

items.question: Which metro route(s), do you think, is/are the best way to reach the zoo from Qutb Minar? ___
steps: The best way is your own opinion, but give a reason from the map. Compare the routes by the stations between and by the changes.
Route A has 14 stations between and 1 change, at Rajiv Chowk.
Route B has 15 stations between and 2 changes, at INA and Mayur Vihar.
Route C has 25 stations between and 2 changes, at Hauz Khas and Botanical Garden.
Route A has the fewest stations and the fewest changes, so it is a good choice.
Check: the reason uses numbers from the map, 14 stations and 1 change.
Your answer may differ: you may choose another route and give your own reason.
items.answer: Sample answer: Route A, because it has the fewest stations (14) and only one change, at Rajiv Chowk. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: Route A, because it has the fewest stations (14) and only one change, at Rajiv Chowk. Your answer may differ.

source: Make a map of a library corner seen from above: 2 shelves on

items.question: Make a map of a library corner seen from above: 2 shelves on the west wall, 1 table with 4 chairs in the middle, and the door on the south wall. Make a key, and hide a bookmark with a red dot.
steps: Draw the floor of the corner from above as a large rectangle. With N at the top, the west wall is the left side and the south wall is the bottom side.
Draw 2 long rectangles along the west wall, one for each shelf. A long rectangle is the symbol for a shelf.
Draw 1 square in the middle for the table and 4 small squares around it for the 4 chairs.
Draw a gap in the south wall for the door.
Hide the bookmark under the table and mark it with a red dot.
Make the key. A long rectangle means shelf. A square with 4 small squares around it means table and chairs. A gap in the wall means door. A red dot means the hidden bookmark.
Read the map to find the bookmark: start at the door on the south wall, walk north to the table, and look under it.
Check: every symbol on the map is in the key, and there is 1 red dot.
items.answer: The map has 2 shelves, a table with 4 chairs and a door, a key that explains each symbol, and a red dot under the table. From the door, walk north to the table to find the bookmark

videos.answer: The map has 2 shelves, a table with 4 chairs and a door, a key that explains each symbol, and a red dot under the table. From the door, walk north to the table to find the bookmark

source: Let Us Do: a map of your school

items.question: Make a map showing the different places in your school. Make a key for the symbols used in the map. Hide some objects in these places. Mark the positions where things are hidden with red dots or flags. Now, challenge your friends to find the hidden things by reading the map.
steps: Choose the places to show. In this sample school there is a gate in the west wall, a road along the west side, a building on the east side, a tree and a bench near the middle, and a garden near the south wall on the west side.

Draw the school from above with N at the top, and draw one symbol for each kind of place. For example a rectangle with two squares for the building, a long rectangle for the bench, a cloud shape for the tree.
Make the key: a small box that shows each symbol with its name, gate, road, building, tree, seat or bench, garden, and the red dot for a hidden object.
Hide 3 objects: one beside the bench, one beside the tree and one in the garden. Mark each place with a red dot.
Write a challenge for a friend: start at the gate and walk east to the tree. The hidden object is a little south of the tree.
Check: every symbol on the map is in the key, there are 3 red dots, and the clue uses only north, east, south and west.
Your map will be different: use your own school, your own symbols and your own clue.

source: An ant starts from its anthill, a grid point of a grid of 1

items.question: An ant starts from its anthill, a grid point of a grid of 1 cm squares. A leaf is 4 squares to the west. A seed is 6 squares to the south. A berry is 2 squares to the east and then 4 squares to the north. How far, and in which direction, must the ant crawl to reach each one?
steps: Each square of the grid is 1 cm. Count the squares along a grid line to find a distance.
Leaf: count 4 squares to the west. The ant crawls 4 cm towards the west.
Seed: count 6 squares to the south. The ant crawls 6 cm towards the south.
Berry: it is not on one straight line. First count 2 squares to the east, then turn and count 4 squares to the north.
The path has two legs: 2 cm towards the east, then 4 cm towards the north.
Length of the path: 2 + 4 = 6 cm.
Check: 4 squares are 4 cm and 6 squares are 6 cm. The two legs of the berry path are 2 squares and 4 squares, and 2 + 4 = 6 squares, which is 6 cm.
items.answer: Leaf: 4 cm towards the west. Seed: 6 cm towards the south. Berry: 2 cm towards the east, then 4 cm towards the north, 6 cm in all

videos.answer: Leaf: 4 cm towards the west. Seed: 6 cm towards the south. Berry: 2 cm towards the east, then 4 cm towards the north, 6 cm in all

source: A berry is 4 cm to the east and 3 cm to the north of the ant

items.question: A berry is 4 cm to the east and 3 cm to the north of the ant. Route 1: 4 cm east, then 3 cm north. Route 2: 3 cm north, then 4 cm east. Route 3: 5 cm east, then 3 cm north, then 1 cm west. Find the length of each route. Which routes are the shortest?
steps: Route 1 has two legs, 4 cm east and 3 cm north. Length: 4 + 3 = 7 cm.
Route 2 has two legs, 3 cm north and 4 cm east. Length: 3 + 4 = 7 cm.
Route 3 has three legs, 5 cm east, 3 cm north and 1 cm west. Length: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 cm.
Routes 1 and 2 are both 7 cm. Route 3 is 9 cm, which is 2 cm longer.
Route 3 goes 1 cm towards the west, away from the berry, and so it also needs 1 cm more towards the east. These two extra steps make the 2 cm.
Check: the berry is 4 cm east and 3 cm north, and 4 + 3 = 7. A route that goes only east and north cannot be shorter than 7 cm.
items.answer: Routes 1 and 2 are 7 cm and are the shortest. Route 3 is 9 cm, because it goes 1 cm the wrong way

videos.answer: Routes 1 and 2 are 7 cm and are the shortest. Route 3 is 9 cm, because it goes 1 cm the wrong way

source: Example 1: the ant and the laddoos

items.question: To get to the laddoos, the ant has to crawl how many cm, and towards which direction?
steps: Each square of the grid is 1 cm. The ant crawls along the grid line that goes from the ant to the plate of laddoos.
Count the squares from the ant to the laddoos: 2 squares, so 2 cm.
Look at the compass. The laddoos are on the right of the ant, on the side of E, so the direction is east.
Check: 2 squares of 1 cm each are 2 cm, and the compass says the right side is east.
items.answer: 2 cm towards the east.

videos.answer: 2 cm towards the east.

source: Anthill in the Zoo: the sugar

items.question: To get to the sugar, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction.
steps: Each square of the grid is 1 cm. Start at the ant.
The sugar is straight above the ant, on the same grid line. Count the squares up to the sugar: 3 squares, so 3 cm.
Look at the compass. N is at the top, so up is north.
The ant crawls 3 cm in the north direction.
Check: 3 squares of 1 cm each are 3 cm, and the arrow on the route points up, towards N.
items.answer: 3 cm in the north direction.

videos.answer: 3 cm in the north direction.

source: Anthill in the Zoo: the bread

items.question: To get to the bread, the ant has to crawl ___ cm in the ___ direction; then ___ cm in the ___ direction.
steps: The bread is not on the same line as the ant, so the route has two legs and turns once.
First leg: count the squares from the ant to the corner of the route on the left: 3 squares, so 3 cm. The left side is the side of W, so the direction is west.
Second leg: at the corner the ant turns and crawls down to the bread: 2 squares, so 2 cm. Down is the side of S, so the direction is south.
The whole path is 3 cm west, then 2 cm south. Its length is 3 + 2 = 5 cm.
Check: the two legs are 3 squares and 2 squares, and 3 + 2 = 5 squares of 1 cm each.
items.answer: 3 cm in the west direction; then 2 cm in the south direction (5 cm in all).

videos.answer: 3 cm in the west direction; then 2 cm in the south direction (5 cm in all).

source: Anthill in the Zoo: the apple

items.question: To get to the apple, the ant needs to crawl ___ cm towards ___, and then ___ cm towards ___, and finally ___ cm towards ___.
steps: The route to the apple is drawn with three legs, so it turns twice.
First leg: count the squares down the grid line from the ant to the corner at the bottom: 5 squares, so 5 cm towards south.
Second leg: at the corner the ant turns and crawls to the right: 3 squares, so 3 cm towards east.
Third leg: it turns again and crawls up to the apple: 2 squares, so 2 cm towards north.
Length of the whole route: 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm.
Check: south 5 cm, east 3 cm, north 2 cm. The three legs are 5, 3 and 2 squares of 1 cm each.
items.answer: 5 cm towards south, 3 cm towards east, and finally 2 cm towards north (10 cm in all).

videos.answer: 5 cm towards south, 3 cm towards east, and finally 2 cm towards north (10 cm in all).

source: Anthill in the Zoo: other routes

items.question: Identify other routes to reach the point where apple is located. Which one is the shortest?
steps: Find where the apple is. It is 3 squares to the right of the ant and 3 squares below it: 3 cm towards the east and 3 cm towards the south.
Route 1: 3 cm towards east, then 3 cm towards south. Length: 3 + 3 = 6 cm.
Route 2: 3 cm towards south, then 3 cm towards east. Length: 3 + 3 = 6 cm.
Route 3: 1 cm towards south, 3 cm towards east, then 2 cm towards south. Length: 1 + 3 + 2 = 6 cm.
The route drawn in your maths book is 5 cm south, 3 cm east and 2 cm north. Length: 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm.
The shortest routes are the 6 cm routes. They go only east and south. The 10 cm route has a step towards the north, away from the apple.
Check: any route made of 3 cm east and 3 cm south, in any order, is 6 cm. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: Sample answer: 3 cm east then 3 cm south, or 3 cm south then 3 cm east. Each is 6 cm, a shortest route. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: 3 cm east then 3 cm south, or 3 cm south then 3 cm east. Each is 6 cm, a shortest route. Your answer may differ.

source: Find the position of the giraffe on the zoo map. Start from

items.question: Find the position of the giraffe on the zoo map. Start from 0, move east to the 8th column, then move north to the 9th row. How do we write the position?
steps: Start at 0, the corner at the bottom left of the grid.
Move east along the bottom line, counting the numbered column lines 1, 2, 3 up to 8. Stop at column 8. That is 8 steps east.
From there move north along the column line, counting the row lines 1, 2, 3 up to 9. Stop at row 9. That is 9 steps north.
The giraffe stands where column 8 and row 9 meet.
Write the column first and the row second: (8,9).
Check: 8 steps east first, then 9 steps north, and the bracket (8,9) lists the column and then the row.
items.answer: The giraffe is at (8,9): 8 steps east, then 9 steps north

videos.answer: The giraffe is at (8,9): 8 steps east, then 9 steps north

source: A child says that the giraffe is at (9,8). Is that right?

items.question: A child says that the giraffe is at (9,8). Is that right?
steps: The giraffe stands at (8,9): 8 steps east, then 9 steps north.
(9,8) means 9 steps east, then 8 steps north. That is a different meeting point.
Walk it on the map: start at 0, move east to column 9, then north to row 8. This is a spot on the path, and no animal stands there.
The first number is the column and the second number is the row, so changing the order changes the place.
Check: (8,9) is the giraffe and (9,8) is not, so (8,9) and (9,8) are not the same place.
items.answer: No. The giraffe is at (8,9). (9,8) is 9 steps east and 8 steps north, a spot with no animal

videos.answer: No. The giraffe is at (8,9). (9,8) is 9 steps east and 8 steps north, a spot with no animal

source: Example 2: reaching the panda

items.question: Start from 0 on the zoo map. How do you reach the panda, and how do we write its position?
steps: Start from 0, the corner at the bottom left of the zoo map.
Move one step horizontally towards the east along the bottom line. You reach the first column.
From there move one step up, towards the north, along the first column line. You reach the first row.
The panda is where the first column and the first row meet.
Write the column number first and the row number second: (1,1).
Check: 1 step east and 1 step north end at the panda, and (1,1) says the same, column 1 and row 1.
items.answer: From 0, move 1 step east to the first column, then 1 step north to the first row. The panda is at (1,1).

videos.answer: From 0, move 1 step east to the first column, then 1 step north to the first row. The panda is at (1,1).

source: Locating the Animals: the tortoise

items.question: To reach the tortoise, move ___ steps towards east and reach the ___ column. Then move ___ step(s) ___ and reach the first ___.
steps: Start from 0 and move horizontally towards the east along the bottom line, counting the numbered column lines: 1, 2, 3, 4.
The tortoise stands on the fourth column line, so move 4 steps towards east and reach the 4th column.
Now move up towards the north. The tortoise is on the first row line, so move 1 step north and reach the first row.
The blanks are: 4 steps, 4th column, 1 step, north, row.
Check: the position of the tortoise is (4,1), the column first and the row second.
items.answer: Move 4 steps towards east and reach the 4th column. Then move 1 step north and reach the first row. The position is (4,1).

videos.answer: Move 4 steps towards east and reach the 4th column. Then move 1 step north and reach the first row. The position is (4,1).

source: Locating the Animals: what is at (1,4)

items.question: The location of the tortoise is (4,1). What is at (1,4)?
steps: The first number of a position is the column and the second number is the row. (4,1) is column 4 and row 1: the tortoise.
(1,4) is column 1 and row 4. Start from 0 and move 1 step east to the first column.
Then move 4 steps north to the fourth row.
Look at the map where the first column and the fourth row meet: a snake lies there.
(1,4) is not the same place as (4,1). The numbers are in a different order, so a different animal is there.
Check: column 1 and row 4 is the snake, and column 4 and row 1 is the tortoise.
items.answer: A snake. (1,4) is 1 step east, then 4 steps north.

videos.answer: A snake. (1,4) is 1 step east, then 4 steps north.

source: Answer the Following: Q1 locate the animal

items.question: Locate the animal at the following positions on the map. (a): (11,11) ___; (b): (2,6) ___; (c): (6,4) ___; (d): (3,10) ___; (e): (11,3) ___; (f): (10,9) ___
steps: For every position, start from 0. The first number tells the steps east to the column. The second number tells the steps north to the row.
Part (a), (11,11): 11 steps east, then 11 steps north. A toucan sits on the tree at the top right corner.
Part (b), (2,6): 2 steps east, then 6 steps north. The animal is a tiger.
Part (c), (6,4): 6 steps east, then 4 steps north. The animal is an elephant.
Part (d), (3,10): 3 steps east, then 10 steps north. The animal is a flamingo.
Part (e), (11,3): 11 steps east, then 3 steps north. The animal is a monkey, on the big tree.
Part (f), (10,9): 10 steps east, then 9 steps north. The animal is a zebra.
Check: each animal stands where its column line and its row line meet.
items.answer: (a): toucan; (b): tiger; (c): elephant; (d): flamingo; (e): monkey; (f): zebra.

videos.answer: (a): toucan; (b): tiger; (c): elephant; (d): flamingo; (e): monkey; (f): zebra.

source: Answer the Following: Q2 write the position

items.question: Write the position of the following animals on the map. (a): Lion ___; (b): Elephant ___; (c): Tortoise ___; (d): Deer ___; (e): Panda ___; (f): Crocodile ___
steps: For each animal, look at the numbers of the lines that meet at it. Read the column number along the bottom and the row number up the side. Write the column first.
Part (a), lion: column 3 and row 3, so (3,3).
Part (b), elephant: column 6 and row 4, so (6,4).
Part (c), tortoise: column 4 and row 1, so (4,1).
Part (d), deer: column 10 and row 6, so (10,6).
Part (e), panda: column 1 and row 1, so (1,1).
Part (f), crocodile: column 10 and row 1, so (10,1).
Check: walk from 0 to each position, east first and then north, and you reach the animal.
items.answer: (a): lion (3,3); (b): elephant (6,4); (c): tortoise (4,1); (d): deer (10,6); (e): panda (1,1); (f): crocodile (10,1).

videos.answer: (a): lion (3,3); (b): elephant (6,4); (c): tortoise (4,1); (d): deer (10,6); (e): panda (1,1); (f): crocodile (10,1).

source: Answer the Following: Q3 place the dots

items.question: Place dots of different colours on the following positions. (a): (8,3) (Red); (b): (2,9) (Green); (c): (7,3) (Blue); (d): (3,8) (Orange); (e): (8,6) (Black); (f): (6,6) (Pink)
steps: For every dot, start from 0, move east to the column, then north to the row, and mark the meeting point.
Part (a), (8,3): 8 steps east, then 3 steps north. Put a red dot there.
Part (b), (2,9): 2 steps east, then 9 steps north. Put a green dot there.
Part (c), (7,3): 7 steps east, then 3 steps north. Put a blue dot there.
Part (d), (3,8): 3 steps east, then 8 steps north. Put an orange dot there.
Part (e), (8,6): 8 steps east, then 6 steps north. Put a black dot there.
Part (f), (6,6): 6 steps east, then 6 steps north. Put a pink dot there.
Check: the six dots are in six different places, and each pair has the column first.
items.answer: Dots at (8,3) red, (2,9) green, (7,3) blue, (3,8) orange, (8,6) black and (6,6) pink.

videos.answer: Dots at (8,3) red, (2,9) green, (7,3) blue, (3,8) orange, (8,6) black and (6,6) pink.
